title: Demon Slayer -Kimetsu no Yaiba- The Movie: Mugen Train
summary: ufotable's 117-minute theatrical continuation of S1 (JP 2020-10-16, 劇場版「鬼滅の刃」無限列車編), and a straight, in-order adaptation of the owner's own manga. ja-WP states it plainly: made 'as the sequel to the TV anime 竈門炭治郎立志編, depicting the Mugen Train battle contained in volumes 7 and 8 of the original comics'. The chapter span is fixed at both ends by two independent instruments. START: MangaUpdates' per-work coverage segments read S1 end 'Vol 7, Chap 54 Page 4' and S2 start 'Vol 7, Chap 54 Page 5', and the Kimetsu no Yaiba Wiki's page-partitioned per-episode fields agree exactly — ep 26 = 'Chapter 51 (p. 12-19), 52, 53 (p. 5-21), 54 (p. 1-4)', ep 28 = 'Chapter 54 (p. 5-19), 55 (p. 1-4, 14-19)'. END: the wiki's ep 33 field is 'Chapter 64 (p. 3-18), 65, 66' and its Mugen Train Arc page gives the arc as chapters 54-66; ja-WP's own film synopsis ends on ch 66's final beat (the Kasugai crows carrying Kyojuro's death to the Hashira, and Kagaya Ubuyashiki's 「寂しくはないよ…」). The run resumes at ch 67 in ep 34. Nothing surprising in the adaptation itself: the alterations sources record are studio expansions inside adapted chapters — a second demon added to Rengoku's Shiranui scene (アニメイトタイムズ, and the wiki's ep 28 note), an extended Enmu fight, extra wounds and a manga-less 'Blazing Universe' form in the Akaza duel, Tanjiro's dream moved to first — plus a short anime-original prologue of Kagaya and Amane Ubuyashiki visiting the Corps graves (ja-WP art section: 「冒頭の墓参りのシーン」). Under T28's faithfulness clause those are divergences on a canon row, not an original share; the manga occupies essentially the whole film. The one genuinely surprising fact is structural, and it is the reason this verdict matters: our rows 27-33 are not a sequel to the film, they ARE the film. ja-WP and the official ufotable/Aniplex/Shueisha statement quoted by AV Watch both say TV episodes 2-7 are the theatrical feature split into six and broadcast with roughly 70 newly added cuts, new BGM, new next-episode previews and new OP/ED visuals, while TV episode 1 (our row 27) is a wholly new anime-original episode; the wiki's film infobox prints the same mapping as 'episodes = 28 - 33'.

chapters_adapted.note: vols 7-8, continuous and in order: ch 54 「こんばんは煉獄さん」 from p. 5 (S1 ep 26 already animated pp. 1-4 — the arrival at the station and Rengoku's bento; MU pins the seam at exactly that page break) through 55-65 to ch 66 「黎明に散る」 in full, closing on Kyojuro's death and the Corps being told of it. NOT counted here: the film's anime-original opening (the Ubuyashikis at the Demon Slayer graves), which carries no chapter, and ch 67+, which the run reaches only in ep 34. Note the arc-boundary variance in sources — the wiki's arc page ends the Mugen Train Arc at ch 66, アニメイトタイムズ extends the manga arc to ch 69 — but the FILM stops at 66 on every reading: 67-69 are ep 34's, per the wiki's ep 34 field (67, 68, 69, 70) and its ch 67 page ('anime episode = 34').

position.why: Right, and provable on pages rather than on air date: ep 26 'New Mission' (the S1 finale) stops at ch 54 p. 4 and the film's first frame of source is ch 54 p. 5 (MU's S1-end / S2-start segments; the wiki's page-partitioned ep 26 and ep 28 fields). Nothing in the run comes between them. THE RELATION TO ROWS 27-33: those rows are the same material re-broadcast, not a continuation — row 27 (TV ep 1, 'Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku') is a wholly anime-original prologue with NO film counterpart (the wiki: 'Episode 27 is entirely anime-original', no chapters field; ja-WP: 完全新作／アニメオリジナルエピソード; and it is the one episode Crunchyroll's Infinity Castle marathon omitted), and rows 28-33 ARE the film, cut into six parts (ja-WP: 「劇場版本編は第2話から第7話として分割され」; the official ufotable/Aniplex/Shueisha statement via AV Watch: 「第2話～第7話は、無限列車での任務を、約70カットの新作追加映像と新規追加BGM、完全新作予告編、新主題歌映像と共に描きます」; the wiki's film infobox: 'episodes = 28 - 33'). So a viewer takes ONE path, never both: 1-26 → the film → 34…, or 1-26 → 27-33 → 34…. 26.5 is correct for either — it places the film where its story begins; a position after row 33 would put a duplicate telling behind its own retelling. DOES THE FILM ADD ANYTHING THE TV CUT LACKS? On story, no — the addition runs the other way. The TV re-telling is a superset: one extra original episode plus ~70 new cuts, new BGM, new previews and new OP/ED, and per a detailed Japanese shot-by-shot comparison (Cinemarche, cross-check tier) the additions include a beat the film had skipped — the tubercular boy leaving Tanjiro's collapsing unconscious domain, redeemed by Tanjiro's warmth, which the manga depicts. No source I found reports any film scene removed for TV; the official statement describes additions only. What the film exclusively has is presentation, not content: one uninterrupted 117-minute cut and its own end-credit roll to LiSA's 「炎」 (kept in the TV path as ep 33's ED). One optional-ordering note: row 27 is chronologically a PREQUEL to the film (Rengoku's mission on the way to the train; the wiki places it 'during the events of Chapter 53'), so a film-path viewer may watch row 27 first if they want it — that is a UI nicety, not a reason to move the stored position.

flags_for_sean: THE ALTERNATIVE-TELLING MARKER (the one thing this row needs beyond a standing). The film at 26.5 and rows 28-33 are the SAME 117 minutes; rows 27-33 are the film plus one original episode. Without a marker the ledger renders the film as an insertion the viewer takes IN ADDITION to the next six rows, which is wrong in both directions — a film-path viewer should be sent from the film to row 34, and a TV-path viewer should be told the film is redundant. Related-works needs an 'alternative to rows N-M' relation (AniList already carries the edge: 112151 ALTERNATIVE → Kimetsu no Yaiba: Mugen Ressha-hen (TV)). Recommended text either way: 'the film and episodes 27-33 tell the same story — watch one; the TV version adds an original prologue episode and ~70 new cuts'.

COVERAGE GAP IN THE RUN, outside this ask but worth a queue entry: the grid I was given shows rows 27, 28 and 29 with EMPTY anchors, i.e. the whole Mugen Train TV block appears unanchored while ep 26 ends at ch 54 and the run picks up again later. The per-episode map exists and is page-partitioned on the wiki, corroborated at the seam by MU: 28 = 54 (p. 5-19), 55 (p. 1-4, 14-19); 29 = 55 (p. 5-13), 56, 57 (p. 1-11, 15-19); 30 = 57 (p. 11-14), 58, 59; 31 = 60, 61, 62 (p. 1-2); 32 = 62 (p. 3-19), 63, 64 (p. 1-2); 33 = 64 (p. 3-18), 65, 66; 34 = 67-70. Two shapes to watch when it is anchored: ch 55 is un-cross-cut across 28/29 (a START back-jump + `rearranged`), and eps 31 and 32 each hand a 2-page tail forward (A47 — END 61 and END 63, tails in chapters_adapted with `partial`). Row 27 takes no anchor (filler, A1).

CONDITIONAL A47 ON EP 26 — do not act yet. Ep 26's stored END is 54, but its share of ch 54 is only pp. 1-4 (MU: S1 ends 'Vol 7, Chap 54 Page 4'), and the next episode that adapts pages, ep 28, STARTS on ch 54 p. 5. If and when rows 28-33 are anchored, ep 26 becomes a textbook A47 hold: END 53, ch 54 (p. 1-4) staying in chapters_adapted with a `partial`. While the block is unanchored no later row owns the tail, so the stored 54 is the honest frontier today. Flagging so the two decisions are made together and the seam does not regress.

ROW 27 CONFIRMED FILLER, and not a side_source: three sources make it anime-original (wiki 'entirely anime-original' with no chapters field; ja-WP 完全新作／アニメオリジナルエピソード; Aniplex of America's own ep 1 synopsis, which describes a mission that exists nowhere in the manga), and its cast is studio-invented (Fuku, Tomi, Tatsu, the 'Slasher' demon). It is NOT an adaptation of Gotoge's Special One-Shot 特別読切／煉獄零話 (19 pp, WSJ 2020 #44, printed in the theatergoers' 煉獄零巻 and later Fanbook 2) — that one-shot is Kyojuro's FIRST mission against a flute demon, and its `anime episode` field is empty. Worth recording before someone joins the two on the Rengoku name. The 84-page 煉獄零巻 itself is a screening giveaway, not film content.

NOT VERIFIED, stated as a gap: whether the film's anime-original grave-visit prologue (ja-WP 「冒頭の墓参りのシーン」; the same scene the Infinity Castle verdict cites Realsound calling the model for that film's opening) survives in TV ep 28. Fan recaps say it does; the wiki's ep 28 cast list omits both Ubuyashikis, which is weak counter-evidence from a user-maintained field. Nothing turns on it for the standing or the position — it is the only candidate for 'something the film has that the TV cut lacks', and no source states any film scene was removed.
